summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of annealing on the microstructure and mechanical properties of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V alloy.
summary_en.method: Specimens were heat-treated under various annealing conditions and subjected to tensile testing and microstructural characterization.
summary_en.result: Annealing tailored the microstructure, improving ductility at the expense of strength.
summary_en.validation: Experimental tensile tests and microscopy were used to correlate mechanical properties with microstructural changes.

papers.title: Probing the Phase Composition and Surface Roughness in the Biological Response of Additively Manufactured Titanium Alloy Bioimplants
papers.abstract: Titanium alloys, mainly Ti-6Al-4V, are renowned for their impressive strength-to-weight ratio and stand as some of the most widely used metallic materials for bioimplants. Additive manufacturing introduces a paradigm shift in the short turnaround times for the availability of such implants. The biological performance of these implants is critical to ensure their success and is understood to be affected by a variety of factors, including surface characteristics and phase composition of the material, often determined by the manufacturing approach. The experimental investigation of the difference in biological performance caused by surface roughness and phase compositions resulting from manufacturing methods that involve laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and hot isostatic pressing (HIP) has been conducted. Surface roughness was found to be the prevailing effect over the reported phase composition difference, with a relatively rougher surface seeming to be better for biological performance in this contribution. Meanwhile, HIP-ed Ti-6Al-4V samples exhibit better cell viability compared to that of the as-built LPBF-ed Ti-6Al-4V samples.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how surface roughness and phase composition, influenced by manufacturing and post-processing, affect the biological performance of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V bioimplants.
summary_en.method: Cell viability assays were conducted on Ti-6Al-4V samples fabricated by laser powder bed fusion and subsequently treated with hot isostatic pressing.
summary_en.result: Surface roughness was found to dominate over phase composition in influencing biological response, with hot isostatic pressed samples showing improved cell viability compared to as-built ones.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed via in vitro cell viability experiments.

papers.title: Prediction and multi-objective optimization of heat affected zone in femtosecond laser machining of Ti-6Al-4V alloy using GA-enhanced machine learning
papers.abstract: Abstract In the manufacture of turbine blade cooling holes for aero-engines, precise control of the heat-affected zone (HAZ) is crucial for ensuring structural integrity, extending service life, and maintaining aerodynamic performance. However, during femtosecond laser drilling of Ti-6Al-4V cooling holes, the HAZ thickness is highly sensitive to processing parameters and exhibits strong nonlinear and multi-factor coupling effects, making its prediction and control particularly challenging. To address this issue, this study proposes a hybrid prediction and optimization approach that integrates machine learning with a genetic algorithm (GA). A Gaussian support vector regression (G-SVR) model is developed to capture the nonlinear relationship between laser parameters and HAZ thickness, while the GA enables multi-objective parameter optimization. The combined G-SVR-GA framework achieves reliable prediction accuracy and provides optimized parameter sets under different objectives, such as minimizing the HAZ thickness or achieving a specified target value. This quantitative and reproducible method offers an effective strategy for HAZ control in femtosecond laser drilling of Ti-6Al-4V cooling holes, providing valuable guidance for precision wall-quality management in the fabrication of critical aero-engine components.

papers.title: Influence of cross-shear and contact stress on the wear of UHMWPE on boost-diffusion-treated additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V
papers.abstract: The more widespread adoption of additive manufacturing (AM) in the biomedical industry has enabled the production of patient-specific implants. When used in joint replacements (or as a bearing material), it is essential to understand the wear behaviour of additively manufactured implants when subjected to loading and motion that simulate their intended use. The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of cross-shear and contact stress on the wear behaviour of ultra-high molecular weight polyethene (UHMWPE) against boost-diffusion-treated (BD-treated) AM Ti-6Al-4V under varying conditions. Multidirectional pin-on-plate wear testing was conducted across cross-shear ratios from 0 to 0.3 and contact stresses ranging from 0.56 to 14 MPa. Surface characterisation techniques were used before and after wear testing to gain insights into the wear mechanisms. The wear of UHMWPE against BD-treated Ti-6Al-4V was compared to that of CoCr and untreated wrought Ti-6Al-4V. Results revealed that against BD-treated Ti-6Al-4V, UHMWPE wear was initially high due to the high surface roughness; however, continued wear testing led to polishing of the BD-treated Ti-6Al-4V, a reduction in the dynamic friction coefficient, and a decrease in wear rate. The high initial surface finish of the BD-treated Ti-6Al-4V resulted from the oxidation heat treatments. However, following wear testing surface degradation was absent, highlighting the potential benefit of the surface treatment in AM patient-specific implants. • Titanium additive manufacturing enables design of complex articulating implants • Boost diffusion can enhance abrasion resistance under multidirectional loading • Surface roughness increases due to the formation of an oxygen enriched rutile layer • Without polishing, roughened topography dominates the tribological response

summary_en.motivation: To understand the wear behavior of additively manufactured implants for joint replacements under varying loading and motion conditions.
summary_en.method: Multidirectional pin-on-plate wear testing was conducted across cross-shear ratios from 0 to 0.3 and contact stresses from 0.56 to 14 MPa.
summary_en.result: Wear of UHMWPE against BD-treated Ti-6Al-4V was initially high due to surface roughness but decreased as polishing occurred, accompanied by a reduction in friction coefficient.
summary_en.validation: Wear results were compared against CoCr and untreated wrought Ti-6Al-4V, and surface characterization was performed before and after testing.
